code.originalText: Diagnosis visit with the endocrinology consultation: A1c, fasting glucose, GAD antibodies, C-peptide, urine albumin, lipids and B12; type 2 diabetes confirmed; metformin by shared decision; nutrition and fasting plans

text.paragraph: Diagnosis visit: fasting test results with the endocrinology consultation. [S]

Swami Vivekananda returns one week after his first visit, fasting since the evening meal, for blood tests drawn this morning and his consultation with Dr. Lindqvist-Bose. He is still thirsty and passes urine three times a night. He has drunk water freely as advised. A few days ago he kept the night-long fast of a major festival, without water until the next morning, and felt light-headed and very thirsty by dawn; he asked how he can keep his fasts safely. His home blood pressure readings over the week averaged 136/86. He wants to know what kind of diabetes this is and whether he will need injections. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1898-02-16; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well, alert and forthright; weight 72.8 kg, BMI 24.6; blood pressure 136/86, pulse 80
No acanthosis nigricans; mucous membranes moist
Skin intact; pulses present; monofilament and vibration sense normal

Thirst, frequent urination day and night, tiredness and about 4 kg weight loss over two months, with a random glucose of 246 mg/dL; told by physicians a year ago that he had diabetes, never confirmed with modern tests or treated except by diet. Diabetes to be confirmed and classified (type 2, type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes) with A1c, fasting glucose, GAD antibodies and C-peptide
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented diabetes of the year before. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Type 2 diabetes: A1c 9.4 percent and fasting glucose 172 mg/dL, with symptoms; GAD65 antibodies negative and fasting C-peptide preserved (2.6 ng/mL); no ketones. BMI 24.6, in the range where ADA screens Asian Americans. Classified as type 2, not type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes
S — Synthetic modern confirmation and classification linked to his documented diabetes.
Moderately increased albuminuria on a first sample (urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 46 mg/g), eGFR normal; to be confirmed on two of three samples over three to six months
S — Synthetic finding linked to his documented albuminuria; superseded when diabetic kidney disease was confirmed.
Raised blood pressure in clinic (138/86, average of two readings) without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings to be taken
S — Synthetic finding; not a claim about his real blood pressure.

Long-standing difficulty falling asleep: by his own account he has never been able to fall asleep on getting into bed and lies awake for two hours or more most nights; worse lately with waking to pass urine; rises before dawn for meditation
S — Synthetic modern problem linked to his documented lifelong difficulty falling asleep.

list.item:
Type 2 diabetes, new (E11.65). Diabetes is confirmed by two abnormal results, A1c 9.4 percent and fasting glucose 172 mg/dL, with symptoms. GAD65 antibodies are negative and the fasting C-peptide of 2.6 ng/mL shows good insulin secretion, so this is type 2 diabetes, not type 1 or slowly progressive autoimmune diabetes; his urine had no ketones. South Asian people develop type 2 diabetes younger and at lower weights, which is why ADA screens Asian Americans from a BMI of 23; his BMI is 24.6. Insulin is not needed now: there is no ketosis, his own insulin is preserved and the A1c is below 10 percent. After discussing metformin alone, metformin with a second tablet, and an injected GLP-1 receptor agonist, he chose to start with metformin and diet and to review in five weeks. [S]
Metformin extended-release 500 mg with the evening meal for a week, then 1000 mg.
Home glucose meter: fasting reading daily, and during any fast.
Dietitian and diabetes education this week.
Target A1c below 7 percent.

Religious fasting with diabetes. Fasting is his practice and his decision. Using IDF-DAR risk stratification adapted to his fasts, his risk is moderate: on metformin alone hypoglycemia is unlikely, but with glucose this high a fast without water risks dehydration, as he felt last week. [S]
Fortnightly fasts with fruit, milk and water are reasonable now; avoid fasts without water until his glucose is steady below 180 mg/dL.
Take metformin with the meal that ends a fast.
Check glucose at midday and before breaking the fast; break the fast if below 70 or above 300 mg/dL, or if dizzy, confused or vomiting.

Moderately increased albuminuria, first sample (R80.9). Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 46 mg/g with a normal eGFR; it can rise with very high glucose, so it must be repeated twice over three to six months. [S]
Repeat at the next visit and in three months.

Raised blood pressure (R03.0). Clinic 136/86 and home 136/86: hypertension is likely; with albuminuria the target is below 130/80. [S]
Decide on treatment at the preventive visit after another week of home readings.

Mixed hyperlipidemia (E78.2). LDL 132, triglycerides 228 and HDL 36; triglycerides will fall as glucose improves. [S]
Discuss a statin at the preventive visit.

Insomnia (G47.00). Lifelong difficulty falling asleep, worse with nocturia from high glucose. [S]
Sleep diary; cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia referral.

Hyperglycemia with thirst and weight loss (R73.9). Explained by the diagnosis made today; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.
